title: Choose the visual world for the PacketMedic landing page
question: The roll assigned the Radiology Reading Room. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Radiology Reading Room
options.lineage: hospital radiology lightboxes: backlit films, film clips, grease-pencil reads
options.thesis: A packet capture is a scan; PacketMedic reads it like a radiologist. The page is a dark reading room where real captures hang on a lightbox as glowing films, and every finding is circled in grease pencil with its verdict. It refuses the dark-SaaS hero with a terminal screenshot.
options.viewport: A wide lightbox switches on (tube flicker) behind one film: the real timeline of the mixed outage+attack sample drawn as an X-ray trace. A grease-pencil ring circles the port-scan burst, labelled ATTACK in red; a second ring around the DNS timeouts, labelled FAULT in blue. Headline on the reading-room wall: Same broken network. Two different diagnoses. Download for Windows and Open the web demo sit as two clipped film tabs under it.
options.risk: Can tip into medical-drama costume if annotations are cute instead of factual; every mark must point at real frames.

raised.raise: One seed drives everything: every film, trace and number on the page is drawn from the same real sample captures, never decorative waveforms.
Lightbox panels sit on a strict modular grid of identical film cells; nothing floats off-module.
Palette law: red, yellow and blue are reserved for ATTACK, SUSPICIOUS and FAULT. No other element may use them.
One film, one statement: each lightbox cell carries exactly one finding or one fact.
Time is the reading axis: every film reads left to right along the capture's real seconds.

options.label: Field Triage Tags
options.lineage: START mass-casualty triage tags: colour bands, tear-off strips, grommets
options.thesis: PacketMedic triages a network like a field medic triages casualties. Each finding is a printed triage tag with its colour strip torn to ATTACK, SUSPICIOUS or FAULT, tied to the evidence.
options.viewport: A stack of triage tags fanned across the viewport, the top tag filled out for the port scan: verdict strip torn at ATTACK, evidence frames handwritten, fix in the notes field. CTAs are the tag's two tear-off stubs.
options.risk: Most familiar reading of 'medic'; the paper ground drifts toward the cream-and-red default unless the card stock stays industrial.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.lineage: nixie-tube lab counters and frequency meters
options.thesis: PacketMedic's numbers as glowing instruments: health score, packets, attacks and faults each own a tube bank that counts up as a real sample is analysed.
options.viewport: A steel instrument panel: four tube banks count up the analysis of the mixed sample (HEALTH 055, ATTACKS 1, FAULTS 1), engraved CTAs below.
options.case: Fuses well for the metrics; loses on explaining WHY a finding is an attack, the product's core claim.
options.risk: Becomes a dashboard of numbers without the explanation that makes PacketMedic different.

options.label: Generative Parametric Identity
options.case: Judges don't recognise a reseeding logo; it says nothing about diagnosis.
options.kept: One seed (the real captures) drives every visual on the page.

options.label: Wiener Werkstätte Showroom
options.case: Luxury showroom has no tie to networks or diagnosis.

options.label: CRT Arcade Pixel Glow
options.case: Hacker-arcade nostalgia undercuts a serious diagnostic tool and reads as a game.
options.kept: Palette as law: verdict colours are reserved.

options.label: Glazier Colour-field Partition
options.case: Calm architecture, no link to packets or verdicts.

options.label: Pickling Brine Calendar
options.case: Food world; no audience identification at all.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer-tool landing page: big headline, terminal screenshot, feature grid, download button.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and two buttons left, pmtui screenshot right, three feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other security-tool page by design.
